rows.evidence: Q1: Section III Results and Figures 4-5 report the authors' own prototype (Arduino setup with soil moisture sensor node) and the sensed soil moisture data; the LED glows while water is supplied until the saved threshold is reached.
rows.notes: The study is a design/prototype demonstration of an IoT soil-moisture-triggered pump controller for a multi-crop plot. It reports only that the sensor node reads moisture and the pump/LED switches on and off against stored crop thresholds. No crop yield, productivity, water use or labour data are measured or compared with any control; the statements in the Conclusion that the system improves water use and increases yield are assertions, not results. The study therefore supports at most a precondition (a functioning automated scheduling device) of the claimed productivity effect, not the effect itself.

notes: Short conference-style paper with heavily paraphrased/garbled English in parts; no quantitative results tables, no statistics, no field trial. Figures referenced (sensed data, Arduino setup) are not legible in the text but their captions indicate only sensor readings and hardware photos.
